req.title: Task description accepts long text
req.statement: The system shall accept task descriptions up to at least 1000 characters.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-032 states the system shall accept task descriptions up to at least 1000 characters. However, inspection of app/schemas.py reveals TaskBase.description has max_length=500, meaning the schema enforces a 500-char cap. Tests must probe: (1) positive — a description well within the schema limit (e.g. 100 chars) succeeds with HTTP 201; (2) boundary — exactly 500 chars (the schema max) succeeds; (3) boundary — 501 chars is rejected with HTTP 422 (schema validation), exposing the gap between the requirement (1000) and implementation (500); (4) negative — a description of 1001 chars is rejected. The boundary tests at 499/500/501 and 999/1000/1001 are critical for mutation resilience, catching off-by-one mutations on the max_length constant. We also assert exact status codes and exact response body fields to kill constant-mutation and comparison-mutation operators.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
import app.database as _db
import app.models as _models

_models.Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=_db.engine)
_models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=_db.engine)

client = TestClient(app)
desc_100 = "A" * 100
payload = {"title": "Test Task", "description": desc_100, "completed": False}
r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
assert r.status_code == 201
body = r.json()
assert "id" in body
assert isinstance(body["id"], int)
assert body["title"] == "Test Task"
assert body["description"] == desc_100
assert body["completed"] == False

def test_create_task_short_description_accepted():
    _models.Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=_db.engine)
    _models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=_db.engine)
    r2 = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Test Task", "description": "A" * 100, "completed": False})
    assert r2.status_code == 201
    b = r2.json()
    assert b["description"] == "A" * 100
    assert b["completed"] == False
    assert b["title"] == "Test Task"
